tut.s.ga-hu.say1: Bitter, simmering rage; personal humiliation. Low and tight, not shouting.
tut.s.ga-hu.say3: Satisfied, faintly amused. The trap is set.
tut.s.ga-hu.say4: Urgent, sharp bark into the darkness; alarmed, but still a commander.
tut.s.gam-nyeong.say1: YELLED at full volume to his men across the dark camp; a deep, heavy, roaring dare with a rough laugh. Not spoken, shouted.
tut.s.gam-nyeong.say2: Scoffing 'hmph', grudging. Sarcastic, then takes the duty.
tut.s.gam-nyeong.say3: Cold outrage; a dangerous, low demand.
tut.s.gam-nyeong.say4: YELLED at full volume on returning from the raid; a deep, booming roar of triumph with a hearty laugh. Not spoken, shouted.
tut.s.gang-yu.say4: Defiant resolve in retreat; unbroken spirit.
tut.s.gwak-ga.say1: Quiet, heavy concern for a dear friend; softened but dignified.
tut.s.gwak-ga.say2: Frail but wry; shallow breath, a faint smile.
tut.s.gwak-ga.say3: Calm last words, almost comforting. Breathy and slow.
tut.s.gwak-ga.say4: Grieving, voice catching. Quiet, not theatrical.
tut.s.gwan-u.say1: Arrogant, mocking roar across the battlefield.
tut.s.gwan-u.say2: Worried, gentle warning to his brother.
tut.s.gwan-u.say3: Called out across the battlefield to the enemy general; deep, heavy, relaxed and belligerent, savoring the fight to come.
tut.s.gwan-u.say4: Back from the battle, unhurried and proud; a deep, booming, self-assured ease, with a warrior's satisfaction.
tut.s.no-suk.say1: Firm, heavy refusal across the meeting table; dominant and unyielding, a general's warning.
tut.s.no-suk.say2: Polite but firm; reasonable, then steel underneath.
tut.s.no-suk.say3: Shouted at full volume, back on his feet and fired up; loud, hearty gratitude, then a booming vow.
tut.s.ma-cho.say2: Serious, calm warning to his cousin.
tut.s.ma-cho.say3: Gravelly, gut-deep bellow across the battlefield at a young rival; hearty, mocking, full power, as if echoing off the hills.
tut.s.bang-deok.say4: Deep, heavy respect for a worthy foe, spoken out on the battlefield; proud, not soft.
tut.s.bang-tong.say1: Slow, brooding, thinking aloud; a ruler weighing a problem.
tut.s.bang-tong.say2: Smooth, flattering persuasion with a hidden smirk.
tut.s.sa-ma-ui.say1: Mocking, lightly amused taunt; calm and cutting.
tut.s.sa-ma-ui.say4: Quiet awe, then a chilling, ambitious calm.
tut.s.seo-seo.say2: Relaxed, unhurried strategist explaining a formation; calm expertise, taking his time, never rushed or chirpy.
tut.s.seo-seo.say4: Calm and composed instruction, unhurried; quiet confidence, not excited.
tut.s.seo-seo.say6: Cold fury, low and demanding; not shouting wildly.
tut.s.seo-seo.say8: Serious and heavy from here on; low, slow, grief held in, torn between lord and mother. Pauses at the ellipsis.
tut.s.seo-seo.say10: Serious, heavy, low vow through clenched grief; bitter resolve, not shouted, not theatrical.
tut.s.seo-seo.say12: Serious, heavy and sorrowful farewell; slow, low, sincere, each word weighed.
tut.s.son-gwon.say2: Loud and hearty, projected across the camp; proud loyalty with a booming laugh at his own scars. Not quiet.
tut.s.son-gwon.say4: Slow, grudging admiration, half to himself, with a faint wry smile.
tut.s.sun-uk.say4: Satisfied, quietly pleased; a cold, knowing smile.
tut.s.yeo-mong.say3: Mildly suspicious, then lazy and dismissive.
tut.s.yeo-po.say3: Raspy, furious, full-throated roar of insult across the field; booming and hearty, ringing out over the battle.
tut.s.yeo-po.say4: Hungry for battle, riding in to join; a deep, booming laugh in the voice, relaxed and eager to fight.
tut.s.yu-bi.say7: Emotional, impassioned plea; voice rising with feeling.
tut.s.yuk-son.say3: A roaring, triumphant shout across the burning field; loud, gleeful, mocking the enemy.
tut.s.jang-bi.say1: Commanding, imperious order across the battlefield.
tut.s.jang-bi.say3: Rough, gravelly and hearty; a big friendly grin and a laugh in the voice, slapping a comrade on the back.
tut.s.jang-bi.say4: The great roar at Changban bridge: gravelly, thunderous, from the gut at full power, shouted across the river to the whole enemy army.
tut.s.jang-bi.say8: Deeply moved, voice choked with emotion.
tut.s.je-gal-ryang.say1: Exultant command; the wind has come.
tut.s.je-gal-ryang.say3: Furious, commanding orders; fierce but in control.
tut.s.je-gal-ryang.say9: Light, amused aside, almost to himself.
tut.s.jo-un.say1: Gentle, soothing whisper to a child, then firm resolve.
tut.s.jo-un.say3: Quiet appreciation of a fine sword.
tut.s.jo-jo.say1: Unhurried and probing over wine; a sly, controlled smile, testing his guest.
tut.s.jo-jo.say2: Careful, modest answer; hiding his true thoughts.
tut.s.jo-jo.say3: Low, slow and knowing; quietly menacing.
tut.s.ju-yu.say8: Wry, pained humor with a chuckle.
tut.s.ha-hu-don.say2: A deep, raw cry of alarm for his brother; heavy and shaken, not thin.
tut.s.heo-jeo.say4: Heavy relief and gratitude, low and sincere.
tut.s.hwang-chung.say1: A deep, heavy, contemptuous sneer at an old enemy; slow and scornful.
turn.seo-seo: Not a battle cry. A sorrowful, heartfelt vow to his captive mother, spoken low and slow with grief in the throat; restrained anguish, resolve through pain.
turn.jang-bi: A raw, gravelly, full-throated bellow challenging the enemy, as if shouting across a valley; hearty and fearless.
turn.ju-tae: A loud, hearty shout as he throws himself in front of his lord; full voice, bold and proud.
turn.jang-ryo: Curt, gruff and unhurried, like a drill instructor taking command; low and rough with cool confidence. Not friendly.
turn.seo-hwang: A short, clipped military command barked at full volume: hard attack on the first syllable, every syllable punched out crisply, then cut off dead. Deep and heavy, disciplined and stern. Do NOT stretch, drag out, sing or trail off any vowel.
turn.gwan-pyeong: A young, bright, eager call to battle; light and clear, not heavy.
turn.gam-nyeong: YELLED at full volume: a deep, roaring battle cry announcing himself; heavy and fearless.
turn.ha-hu-yeon: Urgent and driving, a deep, heavy commander's bark on the march; fast but weighty.
turn.heo-jeo: A short, hearty battle call as he takes his turn: quick, crisp and clipped, cut off cleanly. Not theatrical, not slow.
turn.hwang-chung: A short, hearty battle call as he takes his turn: quick, crisp and clipped, cut off cleanly. Not theatrical, not slow.
turn.beop-jeong: A short, hearty battle call as he takes his turn: quick, crisp and clipped, cut off cleanly. Not theatrical, not slow.
